title: Application version has no single source of truth: hardcoded const drives updates while the assembly says 1.0.0.0
existing_state: The real version exists only as private const ApplicationVersion = "0.51.23" in Form1.cs:115. SSH_Helper.csproj contains no <Version>/<AssemblyVersion>/<FileVersion> property at all (verified — the only Version strings are PackageReference attributes), so the compiled exe's assembly/file version is the default 1.0.0.0 and disagrees with the title bar (Form1.cs:329). Critically, UpdateService is constructed with this const (Form1.cs:374-377) and compares GitHub releases against it — so each release requires manually bumping the const, the git branch name (currently also '0.51.23'), and the GitHub tag in sync. A missed const bump means every user is re-offered the version they already run (update loop) or never offered the next one; meanwhile file-properties/installer tooling sees 1.0.0.0 forever.
recommendation: Add <Version>0.51.23</Version> to SSH_Helper.csproj as the single source (CI can override via -p:Version=). Replace the const with a static property reading Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().GetCustomAttribute<AssemblyInformationalVersionAttribute>() (trimming any +commit suffix) and use it for the title, AboutDialog, NoUpdateDialog, and the UpdateService comparison. Delete the Form1.cs:115 const.
user_benefit: Releases can no longer ship with a stale in-app version that breaks the self-updater for every user, and the exe's file properties finally match the product version.

evidence.note: hand-maintained const is the title and the update-comparison baseline
no Version/AssemblyVersion property anywhere — assembly defaults to 1.0.0.0
